1. (Currently Amended) A method, comprising: inputting database constructs generated by a database optimizer as an input to a trained machine-learning algorithm that has been trained on historical database performance data; obtaining a database operation predictor from the machine-learning algorithm as an output, wherein the database operation predictor comprises a prediction of performance metrics not directly calculable by the database optimizer; modifying at least one of the database constructs based on the database operation predictor producing a modified database construct that differs from predictions made by the database optimizer alone; and processing a database operation with the database constructs and the modified database construct.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein inputting further includes inputting the database constructs as query execution plans for a query, and wherein the machine-learning algorithm applies learned patterns from historical query execution data to generate the database operation predictor.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein inputting further includes identifying at least one database construct as a least cost query execution plan identified from the query execution plans by the database optimizer, and wherein the database operation predictor is generated independently of the least cost designation.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein identifying further includes identifying individual pieces of the least cost query execution plan as: a total number of spools used, cardinality for tables with any intermediate results used, a total number of merge joins, a total number of hash joins, nested loop joins, references for the spools, and costs per database resource assigned by the database optimizer, and wherein the machine-learning algorithm uses said individual pieces to generate predictions that refine or contradict the optimizer's cost estimates.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated Central Process Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation, wherein said estimated CPU execution time is derived from machine-learning analysis rather than direct calculation by the database optimizer.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation, wherein said estimated I/O operations are derived from machine-learning analysis rather than direct calculation by the database optimizer.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for the database operation as the modified database construct.

8. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for execution of a query as the modified database construct.

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a workgroup assigned to the database operation as the modified database construct.

10. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising, storing the database operation predictor in database statistics associated with the database operation and the database constructs, wherein the database operation predictor is stored separately from optimizer-generated statistics.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: training a machine-learning algorithm with database constructs produced by a database optimizer, wherein the training incorporates historical performance data that reveals patterns not captured by the database optimizer's cost model; receiving query execution plans for a query from the database optimizer with a least cost query execution plan identified by the database optimizer for the query; providing the query execution plans as input to the machine-learning algorithm; obtaining as an output a predicted execution time for the query based on the least cost query execution plan, wherein the predicted execution time is generated by the machine-learning algorithm and may differ from the optimizer's estimates; and modifying one of: the least cost query execution plan for the query, a scheduled execution time for the query, and resources that are used to execute the query based on the predicted execution time generated by the machine-learning algorithm.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein providing further includes providing the database tool within a workload scheduler and management component of a database system, wherein the database tool displays machine-learning predictions alongside optimizer-generated plans.

16. (Previously presented) The method of claim 12, wherein training further includes training the machine-learning algorithm as a linear regression-based machine-learning algorithm.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes changing an execution resource of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted query execution time generated by the machine-learning algorithm and a current performance associated with the execution resource, wherein the change is made in response to the machine-learning prediction rather than the optimizer's original resource allocation.

19. (Currently Amended) A system, comprising: a database management system; at least one hardware processor; a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having executable instructions representing a trained machine-learning algorithm that has been trained on historical database performance data; the machine learning algorithm configured to execute on the at least one hardware processor from the non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and to perform processing to: i) receive as input database constructs produced by a database optimizer for a database operation of the database management system; and ii) provide as output a predicted value relevant to one of: one or more of the database constructs and the database operation, wherein the predicted value is generated by machine-learning analysis and represents a prediction not directly provided by the database optimizer; wherein the database management system is configured to process the predicted value to determine whether to modify one of: the one or more database constructs and the database operation before processing the database operation within the database management system, based on a comparison between the predicted value and the optimizer's estimates.

20. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 19, wherein the predicted value is an estimated query execution time for a query generated by the machine-learning algorithm and the database operation is execution of a query execution plan for the query within the database management system, and wherein the estimated query execution time may differ from execution time estimates provided by the database optimizer.
